question: Can recent completed reference devices justify correcting the numerical bias of a frozen model, and can an independent device confirmation beat always applying that same correction?
data: Same newly scored FEMTO offset48 and XJTU fifth offset6 windows as completed-choice (now seen development devices); PHM08 NASA full trajectories, historical 72 service engines and 146 separate reference engines. Across all three sites simulate simultaneous starts, no future labels. Use five equally spaced available snapshots per completed reference device. A label can enter only at a service time strictly after the reference device's terminal time. No service device returns labels.
baseline: Frozen source-only bearing phase tree at both bearing sites. Official original engine checkpoint with SourceCombinations learned only from official fit at PHM08. CatBoost on the same restored input is a mature fixed comparator; bearing adds source median and direct CatBoost.
update: Fit one additive constant equal to the average over completed fitting devices of the mean true-minus-predicted value on their five records. No prewritten device exceptions. Clamp the resulting RUL at zero. No feedback -> use baseline. Assign alternating devices by order of failure (tie by id) to fitting and independent confirmation; confirmation devices are never used to fit. Recompute when strictly earlier failures release.
controls: Always return unaltered baseline, always apply fitted bias, or apply only if device-equal MSE on completed confirmation devices strictly improves on baseline. All start from same baseline, have the same feedback and compute caps. Reference units are common to the three arms in the evaluator; time-to-first-feedback, labels used and switch coverage reported.
gate: Adopt for further blind validation if gated RMSE beats both baseline and always-fit by 1% on each claimed site across at least one engine and one bearing cohort, without worsening worst-device RMSE by more than 1% vs baseline. Compare all fixed arms; report even if a fixed tool wins. No gain over always-fit closes the claim of valuable autonomous gating.
